**What**: Build plugins/dso/hooks/lib/static-defense-lib.sh providing four reusable primitives: (1) staged-.sh enumeration over diff-filter A/C/M/R/T, (2) count-based shrink-only baseline load and diff (reject when post-commit count exceeds recorded baseline; reject removing a baseline entry without removing its source violation), (3) suppression-annotation parsing for `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` and `# bash4-only:` requiring a non-empty non-whitespace token, and (4) diagnostic formatting emitting offending line, remediation string, and originating-ticket citation. The library resolves its own paths via BASH_SOURCE -> readlink -f, never via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.
**Why**: All four hooks are thin wrappers over this library; proving enumeration completeness (sc-7) and bash-3.2 self-compatibility (sc-8) here once avoids divergence and re-implementation across hooks.
**Scope**:
- IN: the shared library file; its enumeration, baseline, suppression, and diagnostic functions; a fixture suite exercising those functions; a bash-3.2-constrained test for the library.
- OUT: the four concrete detection hooks; .pre-commit-config.yaml registration; the known-antipatterns.yaml antipatterns are caught at commit time.","description":"## Description
**What**: Implement plugins/dso/hooks/check-pipefail-grep.sh as a thin wrapper over static-defense-lib.sh that detects both bare-pipeline and command-substitution/subshell forms of `… | grep -q` under `set -o pipefail`, ships its initial per-hook baseline capturing the ~63 current violations, and registers in .pre-commit-config.yaml between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate. This is the first hook end-to-end and proves the full pattern (detection + baseline + diagnostics + suppression + fixture + dogfood) before replication.
**Why**: SIGPIPE-under-pipefail is the highest-volume and growing class (~63 files, up from 42); blocking new instances stops growth while the shrink-only baseline lets the backlog through.
**Scope**:
- IN: the hook, its detection logic for both forms, its initial baseline, its .pre-commit-config.yaml entry, and its fixture + end-to-end test.
- OUT: remediation of the ~63 existing violations; the other three hooks; the shared library functions (consumed from draft-1).","priority":0,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":true,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["check-pipefail-grep.sh, when staged content adds a `… | grep -q` under pipefail in bare-pipeline form or command-substitution/subshell form, blocks the commit and the other form is also detected ← Satisfies: sc-1","check-pipefail-grep.sh reads its per-hook count-based baseline so the captured existing violations do not block, while a new instance beyond the baseline count is blocked ← Satisfies: sc-2","check-pipefail-grep.sh emits a per-file diagnostic naming the offending line, the remediation string, and the SIGPIPE originating-ticket citation ← Satisfies: sc-3","check-pipefail-grep.sh honors a `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` suppression with a non-empty token and rejects an empty or whitespace-only suppression reason ← Satisfies: sc-5","a fixture test asserts detection on staged content, baselined-violation non-firing, new-instance blocking, and baseline-growth rejection; **What**: Implement plugins/dso/hooks/check-hermeticity.sh as a thin wrapper over static-defense-lib.sh that detects $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT (and equivalent plugin-root variables) referenced unbound under `set -u`, ships its initial per-hook baseline, and registers in .pre-commit-config.yaml between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate.
**Why**: The unbound-$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT chain recurred across fe45-0b58, 09d8-11f0, 82ad-7bb3, and 97a7-4504 over months; a dedicated hermeticity gate stops the chain.
**Scope**:
- IN: the hook, its detection logic, its initial baseline, its .pre-commit-config.yaml entry, and its fixture + end-to-end test.

**What**: Implement plugins/dso/hooks/check-config-key-docs.sh as a thin wrapper over static-defense-lib.sh that detects a config key added to dso-config.conf without a paired entry in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, ships its initial per-hook baseline, and registers in .pre-commit-config.yaml between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate.
**Why**: Config-doc drift (a190-d780) escapes pre-commit and is only caught post-merge; a dedicated gate keeps config keys and their documentation paired.
**Scope**:
- IN: the hook, its key-pairing detection logic, its initial baseline, its .pre-commit-config.yaml entry, and its fixture + end-to-end test.
- OUT: backfilling docs for existing unpaired keys; the shared library functions (consumed from draft-1).","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["check-config-key-docs.sh blocks a commit when staged content adds a dso-config.conf key that has no paired entry in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md ← Satisfies: sc-1","check-config-key-docs.sh reads its per-hook count-based baseline so captured existing unpaired keys do not block while a new unpaired key beyond the baseline is blocked ← Satisfies: sc-2","check-config-key-docs.sh emits a per-file diagnostic naming the offending key, the remediation string, and the a190-d780 citation ← Satisfies: sc-3","check-config-key-docs.sh honors a non-empty `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` suppression and rejects an empty or whitespace-only suppression reason ← Satisfies: sc-5","a fixture test asserts detection on staged content, baselined-violation non-firing, new-instance blocking, and baseline-growth rejection; **What**: Ship plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml as an append-only registry with a documented versioned schema (id, pattern, target languages/dirs, remediation, citation), document it in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and implement plugins/dso/hooks/check-known-antipatterns.sh as a thin wrapper over static-defense-lib.sh that reads the registry via a single pinned parser (python3 or yq, parser choice independent of yq v3-vs-v4 syntax), blocks staged content matching any registry entry (seeded with the declare -A bash-4-only class), enforces the append-only contract (reject removal or mutation of an existing entry), ships its per-hook baseline, and registers in .pre-commit-config.yaml between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate.
**Why**: The registry is the data-driven extension point consumed by downstream epics (99f1-153c, d63f-2c74, a47f-b451); it must publish a stable versioned schema and tolerate the empty-registry case before those consumers run.
**Scope**:
- IN: the registry file and its versioned schema, the CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md documentation, the hook, the append-only mechanical guard, the pinned-parser choice, the initial baseline, the .pre-commit-config.yaml entry, and the fixture + end-to-end test.
- OUT: populating the registry beyond the seed entry (owned by 99f1-153c); downstream consumer wiring.","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["check-known-antipatterns.sh blocks a commit when staged content matches a registry entry (seed: declare -A in a bash-3.2-target script) read from known-antipatterns.yaml ← Satisfies: sc-1","known-antipatterns.yaml ships as an append-only registry with a documented versioned schema carrying id, pattern, target languages/dirs, remediation, and citation fields, documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and a commit that removes or mutates an existing registry entry is rejected ← Satisfies: sc-4","check-known-antipatterns.sh reads its per-hook count-based baseline so captured existing violations do not block while a new instance beyond the baseline is blocked ← Satisfies: sc-2","check-known-antipatterns.sh emits a per-file diagnostic naming the offending line, the remediation string, and the registry-entry citation ← Satisfies: sc-3","check-known-antipatterns.sh honors a non-empty `# bash4-only:` or `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` suppression and rejects an empty or whitespace-only suppression reason ← Satisfies: sc-5","a fixture test asserts detection on staged content, baselined-violation non-firing, new-instance blocking, and baseline-growth rejection;
